title: Ang 1197: Sarang begins
hookLine: Guru Ram Das opens the midday raga
tomorrow: how does a hymn cool someone down in the middle of a fight?

cards: Noon in a heat wave. The sidewalk shimmers. The car's steering wheel is too hot to hold.
Your shadow has shrunk to a puddle under your feet, and the only thought in your head is water, cold, now. Thirst at midday doesn't negotiate.
On ang 1197 a new raga begins, Sarang, the raga tradition sets for the middle of the day. So what does the Granth sing when the sun is highest?

teach.h: MAHALA 4: MY SUPPORT, DAY AND NIGHT.
teach.b: In the fourth Guru's Sarang hymns, under the heading Mahala 4, the mind is told to repeat the Name of the Lord of the world, and the hymn says, in paraphrase: the Lord is my support, all day and all night.
At midday that word, support, lands differently. It's what you want when the heat is pressing down: a wall to lean on, shade, something cool in your hand.
The Name, in the Granth's language, is amrit, nectar, the drink that doesn't run out. Here's something to tell a friend tonight, and it's a thing you can actually taste.
In summer heat, Sikhs set up a chhabeel: a stand by the road serving cold sweetened water, or a milky drink, free, to anyone passing. Drivers pull over. Kids carry trays to car windows.
Nobody asks who you are or what you believe before handing you a cup.
It's the midday raga turned into something you can hold: a cool thing, given at the hottest hour, to whoever's thirsty. Midday is when shade matters most, and when the hymns say the Name does too.

how: Ragis sing Sarang hymns in kirtan; in summer, Sikh families and gurdwaras set up a chhabeel by the road, handing out cold sweetened water or a milky drink to anyone passing.

games.q: you're running a cold-water stand outside your building in a heat wave. a stranger hesitates: "is this for, like, members?" what fits the midday raga?
o: hand him a cup: it's for whoever's thirsty, no questions.
ask where he's from first, then decide.
point him to the store; the water's for the community.
games.why: a chhabeel is a cool thing given at the hottest hour to anyone passing, the way the hymns hold out the Name as amrit.

practice: Pour a glass of cool water and take one slow sip. Hold it in your mouth for a moment before you swallow, and feel the cold travel down. Then sit with the glass in both hands and let the coolness be the whole practice.
If you'd like, read ang 1197 before you begin.
